title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Charge Transfer
text:
Electric Charge Transfer

Key terms: electric charge, rubbing, electrons

Electric charge is transferred from one body to another when they are rubbed together, causing them to become charged. This transfer involves electrons, which are less tightly bound in some atoms, moving from one body to another.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Charge Transfer in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Conductors and Insulators
text:
Conductors and Insulators

Key terms: conductors, insulators, electricity

Conductors allow electricity to pass through them easily, while insulators resist the passage of electricity. When charged, conductors distribute the charge over their surface, while insulators keep the charge at the same place.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conductors and Insulators in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Additivity of Charges
text:
Additivity of Charges

Key terms: additivity, charge, magnitude

The total charge of a system containing multiple point charges is obtained by adding the charges together algebraically. Charge has magnitude but no direction, similar to mass, but it can be either positive or negative.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Additivity of Charges in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Conservation of Charge
text:
Conservation of Charge

Key terms: conservation, charge, isolated system

Charge is neither created nor destroyed in an isolated system. When bodies are charged by rubbing, the total charge of the system remains constant, as the charge gained by one body is equal to the charge lost by the other.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conservation of Charge in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Quantisation of Charge
text:
Quantisation of Charge

Key terms: quantisation, charge, e

All free charges are integral multiples of a basic unit of charge, denoted by e. This means that charge is quantised, and can only take on discrete values. The charge on an electron is –e, and the charge on a proton is +e.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Quantisation of Charge in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law
text:
Coulomb's Law

Key terms: Coulomb's law, force, point charges

Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. The force is along the line joining the charges and is repulsive if the charges are of the same type and attractive if they are of opposite types.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Coulomb's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law
text:
Coulomb's Law

Key terms: Coulomb's law, point charges, force, distance, charge

Coulomb's law states the force between two point charges. It varies inversely with the square of the distance between them and is directly proportional to the product of the charges.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Coulomb's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law Vector Form
text:
Coulomb's Law Vector Form

Key terms: Coulomb's law, vector notation, force, charge

Coulomb's law can be written in vector notation, where the force on one charge due to another is given by a vector quantity.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Coulomb's Law Vector Form in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Superposition Principle
text:
Superposition Principle

Key terms: superposition principle, force, charge

The superposition principle states that the total force on a charge due to multiple charges is the vector sum of the forces due to each charge individually.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Superposition Principle in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law and Newton's Law
text:
Coulomb's Law and Newton's Law

Key terms: Coulomb's law, Newton's law, electrostatic force, gravitational force

Coulomb's law for electrostatic force and Newton's law for gravitational force both have an inverse-square dependence on distance, but the strength of the electrical force is much greater.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Coulomb's Law and Newton's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law and Acceleration
text:
Coulomb's Law and Acceleration

Key terms: Coulomb's law, acceleration, electrical force, Newton's second law

Using Coulomb's law, the acceleration of a charged particle due to an electrical force can be calculated using Newton's second law of motion.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Coulomb's Law and Acceleration in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law and Charge Distribution
text:
Coulomb's Law and Charge Distribution

Key terms: Coulomb's law, charge distribution, force measurement

When charges are redistributed among identical uncharged spheres, the charge on each sphere is equal, allowing for the measurement of forces at different separations and charges.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Coulomb's Law and Charge Distribution in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law and Force Between Multiple Charges
text:
Coulomb's Law and Force Between Multiple Charges

Key terms: Coulomb's law, multiple charges, force, superposition principle

The force on a charge due to multiple charges is the vector sum of the forces due to each charge individually, according to the superposition principle.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Coulomb's Law and Force Between Multiple Charges
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Coulomb's Law and Force Between Multiple Charges in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Coulomb's Law
text:
Coulomb's Law

Key terms: Coulomb's Law, point charges, force, distance

The force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. The force acts along the line connecting the charges.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Coulomb's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field
text:
Electric Field

Key terms: electric field, force, charge, position, vector

The electric field at a point in space is defined as the force per unit charge experienced by a test charge placed at that point. It is a vector quantity that varies with position and is independent of the test charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field Lines
text:
Electric Field Lines

Key terms: electric field lines, electric field, charges

Electric field lines are a visual representation of the electric field, with the number of lines being proportional to the strength of the field. They always start from positive charges and end at negative charges.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Field Lines in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Superposition Principle
text:
Superposition Principle

Key terms: superposition principle, electric field, force, charges

The electric field due to multiple charges is the vector sum of the electric fields due to each charge individually. This principle also applies to forces.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Superposition Principle in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Uniform Electric Field
text:
Uniform Electric Field

Key terms: uniform electric field, charged plates, magnitude, direction

A uniform electric field has the same magnitude and direction at all points in space. It is produced by two parallel charged plates.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Uniform Electric Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Potential Energy
text:
Electric Potential Energy

Key terms: electric potential energy, work, charges, scalar

The electric potential energy of a system of charges is the work done in assembling the charges from infinity to their final positions. It is a scalar quantity.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Potential Energy in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Potential
text:
Electric Potential

Key terms: electric potential, work, charge, scalar

Electric potential is the amount of work done per unit charge in moving a charge from infinity to a specific point. It is a scalar quantity and is equal to the electric potential energy per unit charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Potential in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Potential Energy and Potential
text:
Electric Potential Energy and Potential

Key terms: electric potential energy, electric potential, charge, center

The electric potential energy of a system of charges is equal to the negative of the product of the total charge and the electric potential at the center of charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Potential Energy and Potential in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Density of Field Lines
text:
Density of Field Lines

Key terms: Field Lines, Electric Field Strength

The number of field lines per unit area indicates the strength of the electric field. More lines mean stronger field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Density of Field Lines in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Field Lines and Charge
text:
Field Lines and Charge

Key terms: Positive Charge, Negative Charge, Electric Field Strength

Field lines start from positive charges and end at negative charges. They crowd where the field is strong and are spaced apart where it is weak.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Field Lines and Charge in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Flux
text:
Electric Flux

Key terms: Electric Field, Electric Flux, Field Lines

Electric flux is the number of field lines crossing a unit area placed normal to the field at a point. It's proportional to the electric field strength.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Flux in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Dipole
text:
Electric Dipole

Key terms: Electric Dipole, Dipole Moment, Electric Field

An electric dipole is a pair of equal and opposite charges. The electric field of a dipole falls off faster than 1/r^2 at large distances.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electric Dipole in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Polar vs Non-Polar Molecules
text:
Polar vs Non-Polar Molecules

Key terms: polar molecule, non-polar molecule, dipole moment

In polar molecules, the centers of negative and positive charges do not coincide, giving them a permanent electric dipole moment. Non-polar molecules have their centers of charge coincide, resulting in no permanent dipole moment.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Polar vs Non-Polar Molecules in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field of a Dipole
text:
Electric Field of a Dipole

Key terms: dipole, electric field, dipole moment

The electric field of a dipole at a far-away point on its axis is given by E = p/(4πε₀r³), where p is the dipole moment and r is the distance from the dipole. The direction is along the dipole moment vector.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Field of a Dipole in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Torque on a Dipole in an Electric Field
text:
Torque on a Dipole in an Electric Field

Key terms: dipole, electric field, torque

A dipole in a uniform external electric field experiences a torque given by τ = p × E, which tends to align the dipole with the field. The magnitude of the torque is pE sinθ, where θ is the angle between the dipole moment and the field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Torque on a Dipole in an Electric Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Torque on a Dipole in an Electric Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Continuous Charge Distribution
text:
Continuous Charge Distribution

Key terms: charge density, linear charge distribution, surface charge distribution, volume charge distribution

Continuous charge distributions are modeled using charge densities: linear (λ), surface (σ), and volume (ρ). The electric field due to a continuous charge distribution is found using Coulomb's law and the superposition principle.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Continuous Charge Distribution in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Gauss's Law
text:
Gauss's Law

Key terms: Gauss's law, electric flux, closed surface, enclosed charge

Gauss's law states that the total electric flux through a closed surface is equal to the total charge enclosed by the surface divided by the permittivity of free space (ε₀). It is a powerful tool for solving electrostatic problems with symmetry.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Gauss's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Gauss's Law for Electric Fields
text:
Gauss's Law for Electric Fields

Key terms: electric flux, Gauss's law, permittivity of free space

States that the total electric flux out of a closed surface is equal to the charge enclosed divided by the permittivity of free space. Used to find electric fields from charge distributions.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gauss's Law for Electric Fields in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet
text:
Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet

Key terms: uniformly charged, infinite plane sheet, surface charge density

The electric field is constant in magnitude and direction, perpendicular to the sheet, and given by E = s/2ε0, where s is the surface charge density.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Infinite Plane Sheet in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Thin Spherical Shell
text:
Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Thin Spherical Shell

Key terms: uniformly charged, thin spherical shell, electric field

Outside the shell, the field is as if all the charge were concentrated at the center. Inside the shell, the field is zero.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Thin Spherical Shell
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electric Field from a Uniformly Charged Thin Spherical Shell in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field from an Infinitely Long Straight Wire
text:
Electric Field from an Infinitely Long Straight Wire

Key terms: infinitely long wire, linear charge density, radial electric field

The electric field is radial, with magnitude E = λ/(2πε0r), where λ is the linear charge density.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Electric Field from an Infinitely Long Straight Wire
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Field from an Infinitely Long Straight Wire in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Violation of Gauss's Law Indicates Departure from Inverse Square Law
text:
Violation of Gauss's Law Indicates Departure from Inverse Square Law

Key terms: Gauss's law, inverse square law, non-uniform charge distribution

Any violation of Gauss's law implies that the electric field does not follow the inverse square law, indicating a non-uniform charge distribution.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Violation of Gauss's Law Indicates Departure from Inverse Square Law
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Violation of Gauss's Law Indicates Departure from Inverse Square Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Flux through a Cube with Non-Uniform Electric Field
text:
Electric Flux through a Cube with Non-Uniform Electric Field

Key terms: electric flux, non-uniform electric field, Gauss's law

The net electric flux through the cube is calculated by summing the fluxes through each face, taking into account the angle between the electric field and the normal to the face.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Electric Flux through a Cube with Non-Uniform Electric Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Flux through a Cube with Non-Uniform Electric Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field and Charge within a Cube with Non-Uniform Electric Field
text:
Electric Field and Charge within a Cube with Non-Uniform Electric Field

Key terms: electric field, charge, Gauss's law, non-uniform electric field

The electric field and charge within the cube are found using Gauss's law, with the flux calculated from the electric field components and the surface area of the cube.

Electric Field

The electric field at a point is the force per unit charge on a small positive test charge placed at that point.

text:
Electric Field Lines

Key terms: electric field lines, electric field, direction

Electric field lines are curves that indicate the direction of the electric field at any point in space.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electric Field Lines in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Dipole

Electric Dipole

Key terms: electric dipole, dipole moment, charge

An electric dipole is a pair of equal and opposite charges separated by some distance, with a dipole moment vector pointing from the negative to the positive charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Electric Dipole in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Gauss's Law
text:
Gauss's Law

Key terms: Gauss's Law, electric field, flux, charge

The flux of the electric field through any closed surface is equal to the total charge enclosed by that surface, divided by the permittivity of free space.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Gauss's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential Energy Definition
text:
Potential Energy Definition

Key terms: potential energy, work, external force

Potential energy is the work done by an external force in moving a body against a force like spring or gravitational force. It's stored energy that can be converted into kinetic energy.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Potential Energy Definition in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Conservative Forces
text:
Conservative Forces

Key terms: conservative forces, work, path independence

Conservative forces are those where the work done in moving a body from one point to another depends only on the initial and final positions, not the path taken. Examples include spring and gravitational forces.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conservative Forces in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatic Potential Energy
text:
Electrostatic Potential Energy

Key terms: electrostatic potential energy, work, electric field

Electrostatic potential energy is the work done by an external force in moving a charge against an electric field. It's the potential energy of a charge in an electric field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electrostatic Potential Energy in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatic Potential
text:
Electrostatic Potential

Key terms: electrostatic potential, work, electric field

Electrostatic potential is the work done per unit test charge in bringing it from infinity to a point in an electric field. It's a measure of the potential energy per unit charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electrostatic Potential in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential Due to a Point Charge
text:
Potential Due to a Point Charge

Key terms: potential, point charge, distance

The potential at a point due to a point charge is directly proportional to the charge and inversely proportional to the distance from the charge. It's given by the formula V = kQ/r.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential Due to a Point Charge
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Potential Due to a Point Charge in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential due to a system of charges
text:
Potential due to a system of charges

Key terms: superposition principle, electrostatic potential

The potential at a point due to multiple charges is the algebraic sum of the potentials due to each individual charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential due to a system of charges
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Potential due to a system of charges in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential due to continuous charge distribution
text:
Potential due to continuous charge distribution

Key terms: charge density, integration

For a continuous charge distribution, the potential is determined by summing (or integrating) the contributions from small volume elements.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential due to continuous charge distribution
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Potential due to continuous charge distribution in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential outside and inside a charged shell
text:
Potential outside and inside a charged shell

Key terms: spherical shell, electric field

Outside a charged spherical shell, the potential is as if all the charge is concentrated at the center. Inside, the potential is constant.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential outside and inside a charged shell
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Potential outside and inside a charged shell in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Zero potential point between two charges
text:
Zero potential point between two charges

Key terms: electric potential, charge

The electric potential is zero at points on the line joining two charges where the potentials due to each charge cancel out.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Zero potential point between two charges
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Zero potential point between two charges in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Equipotential surfaces
text:
Equipotential surfaces

Key terms: electric field, potential

Equipotential surfaces are surfaces with a constant value of potential at all points on the surface, and are normal to the electric field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Equipotential surfaces in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Relation between electric field and potential
text:
Relation between electric field and potential

Key terms: electric field, potential

The electric field is in the direction of steepest decrease in potential, and its magnitude is given by the change in potential per unit displacement normal to the equipotential surface.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Relation between electric field and potential
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Relation between electric field and potential in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential energy of a system of charges
text:
Potential energy of a system of charges

Key terms: potential energy, work

The potential energy of a system of charges is the work done in assembling the charges from infinity to their given locations.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential energy of a system of charges
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Potential energy of a system of charges in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential energy in an external field
text:
Potential energy in an external field

Key terms: external field, potential energy

The potential energy of a charge in an external field is the work done by the external field in bringing the charge from infinity to its current location.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential energy in an external field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Potential energy in an external field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential Energy of Charge in External Field
text:
Potential Energy of Charge in External Field

Key terms: potential energy, external field, electrostatic potential

The potential energy of a charge in an external field is the work done in bringing the charge from infinity to the point of interest. It's calculated using the formula qV, where q is the charge and V is the external potential at that point.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential Energy of Charge in External Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Potential Energy of Charge in External Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential Energy of Two Charges in External Field
text:
Potential Energy of Two Charges in External Field

Key terms: potential energy, system of charges, external field

The potential energy of a system of two charges in an external field is the sum of the work done in bringing each charge from infinity to its respective position, plus the work done against the field due to the other charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential Energy of Two Charges in External Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Potential Energy of Two Charges in External Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Potential Energy of Dipole in External Field
text:
Potential Energy of Dipole in External Field

Key terms: potential energy, dipole, external field, torque

The potential energy of a dipole in an external field is the work done by the external torque in rotating the dipole from an initial angle to a final angle against the torque due to the field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Potential Energy of Dipole in External Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Potential Energy of Dipole in External Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
text:
Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance

Key terms: electrostatic potential, capacitance, work done

Electrostatic potential is the work done per unit charge in bringing a test charge from infinity to a point in the field. Capacitance is the ratio of the charge on a conductor to its potential.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatics of Conductors
text:
Electrostatics of Conductors

Key terms: electrostatic field, conductor, electrostatic potential

In a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero inside and normal to the surface at every point. The interior of a conductor can have no excess charge, and the electrostatic potential is constant throughout the volume of the conductor.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrostatics of Conductors in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Field at Surface of Charged Conductor
text:
Electric Field at Surface of Charged Conductor

Key terms: electric field, surface charge density, permittivity

The electric field at the surface of a charged conductor is normal to the surface at every point and is given by the formula E = σ/ε₀, where σ is the surface charge density and ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Electric Field at Surface of Charged Conductor
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electric Field at Surface of Charged Conductor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatic Shielding
text:
Electrostatic Shielding

Key terms: electrostatic shielding, conductor, electric field

A conductor with a cavity shields the interior from external electric influence, meaning the electric field inside the cavity is always zero.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electrostatic Shielding in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatic Shielding
text:
Electrostatic Shielding

Key terms: conductor, cavity, shielding, electric field

A neutral conductor with a cavity remains shielded from outside electric influence, with zero field inside.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electrostatic Shielding in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Charge Induction
text:
Charge Induction

Key terms: charge, induction, polarization, molecules

Charges on a comb can induce a net force of attraction on small bits of paper due to molecular polarization.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Charge Induction in Grade 12 Physics.

Dielectric Polarization

Key terms: dielectric, polarize, dipole moment, electric field

Dielectrics develop a net dipole moment in an external electric field, reducing the field inside them.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Dielectric Polarization in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitance Definition
text:
Capacitance Definition

Key terms: capacitance, charge, potential difference, capacitor

Capacitance (C) is the ratio of the charge (Q) to the potential difference (V) between the conductors of a capacitor, C = Q/V.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Capacitance Definition in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Parallel Plate Capacitor
text:
Parallel Plate Capacitor

Key terms: parallel plate capacitor, capacitance, area, separation, dielectric constant

A parallel plate capacitor's capacitance (C) is given by C = ε₀A/d, where A is the area of the plates and d is the separation.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Parallel Plate Capacitor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Dielectric Effect on Capacitance
text:
Dielectric Effect on Capacitance

Key terms: dielectric, capacitance, dielectric constant, increase

A dielectric inserted between the plates of a capacitor increases its capacitance, with the increase depending on the dielectric constant (εr) of the material.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Dielectric Effect on Capacitance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitance and Capacitors
text:
Capacitance and Capacitors

Key terms: capacitance, capacitor, dielectric

Capacitance is the ability of a body to store an electrical charge. A capacitor is a device that stores electrical charge temporarily. It consists of two conductors separated by an insulator (dielectric).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Capacitance and Capacitors in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitance Formula
text:
Capacitance Formula

Key terms: capacitance, permittivity, area, distance

The capacitance (C) of a parallel plate capacitor is given by the formula C = ε₀A/d, where ε₀ is the permittivity of free space, A is the area of the plates, and d is the distance between them.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Capacitance Formula in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Dielectric Constant
text:
Dielectric Constant

Key terms: dielectric constant, permittivity, capacitance

The dielectric constant (K) of a material is the factor by which the capacitance of a capacitor increases when the material is inserted between its plates. It is the ratio of the permittivity of the material to the permittivity of free space.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Dielectric Constant in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Series Combination of Capacitors
text:
Series Combination of Capacitors

Key terms: series, capacitance, combination

In a series combination of capacitors, the total capacitance (C) is given by the formula 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + ... + 1/Cₙ, where C₁, C₂, ..., Cₙ are the individual capacitances.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Series Combination of Capacitors in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Parallel Combination of Capacitors
text:
Parallel Combination of Capacitors

Key terms: parallel, capacitance, combination

In a parallel combination of capacitors, the total capacitance (C) is given by the formula C = C₁ + C₂ + ... + Cₙ, where C₁, C₂, ..., Cₙ are the individual capacitances.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Parallel Combination of Capacitors in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Energy Stored in a Capacitor
text:
Energy Stored in a Capacitor

Key terms: energy, capacitor, charge, potential difference

The energy (U) stored in a capacitor is given by the formula U = (1/2)QV or U = (1/2)CV², where Q is the charge stored, V is the potential difference across the capacitor, and C is the capacitance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Energy Stored in a Capacitor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Dielectric Material Increases Capacitance
text:
Dielectric Material Increases Capacitance

Key terms: dielectric, capacitance, dielectric constant

A dielectric material placed between the plates of a capacitor reduces the electric field inside, thus increasing the capacitance. The new capacitance is K times the original, where K is the dielectric constant.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dielectric Material Increases Capacitance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Series and Parallel Capacitor Combinations
text:
Series and Parallel Capacitor Combinations

Key terms: series, parallel, capacitance, total capacitance

In series, the total capacitance is the reciprocal of the sum of reciprocals of individual capacitances. In parallel, the total capacitance is the sum of individual capacitances.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Series and Parallel Capacitor Combinations in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Energy Stored in a Capacitor
text:
Energy Stored in a Capacitor

Key terms: energy, capacitor, charge, voltage, capacitance

The energy stored in a capacitor is given by the formula U = QV or U = 0.5CV^2, where Q is the charge, V is the voltage, and C is the capacitance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Energy Stored in a Capacitor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Energy Density
text:
Electric Energy Density

Key terms: energy density, electric field, permittivity

The electric energy density in a region with an electric field is (1/2)e0E^2, where e0 is the permittivity of free space and E is the electric field strength.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electric Energy Density in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrostatic Shielding
text:
Electrostatic Shielding

Key terms: shielding, cavity, conductor, electrostatic

A cavity inside a conductor is shielded from external electrical influences, but charges inside the cavity do not shield the exterior of the conductor.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electrostatic Shielding in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Potential and Energy
text:
Electric Potential and Energy

Key terms: potential energy, electric field, electric potential

The potential energy of a charge q in an electric field is qV(r), where V(r) is the potential due to external charges, not including the potential due to q itself.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electric Potential and Energy in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitor with Dielectric
text:
Capacitor with Dielectric

Key terms: dielectric, capacitor, voltage, charge

When a dielectric material is inserted between the plates of a capacitor, the capacitance increases, and if the capacitor is connected to a voltage source, the charge on the plates remains constant, but the voltage across them decreases.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Capacitor with Dielectric in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Energy Transfer in Capacitor Circuit
text:
Energy Transfer in Capacitor Circuit

Key terms: energy transfer, capacitor, circuit

When two capacitors are connected, energy can be transferred from one to another. If the capacitors have the same capacitance, the energy is equally shared between them.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Energy Transfer in Capacitor Circuit in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electric Current Definition
text:
Electric Current Definition

Key terms: electric charge, current, rate of flow

Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge. It's defined as the net charge flowing across a cross-section of a conductor per unit time.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electric Current Definition in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ohm's Law
text:
Ohm's Law

Key terms: Ohm's law, current, potential difference, resistance

Ohm's law states that the current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) applied across it, and inversely proportional to its resistance (R). Mathematically, V = IR.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ohm's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Resistance and Conductance
text:
Resistance and Conductance

Key terms: resistance, conductance, electric current

Resistance (R) is the opposition to the flow of electric current. Conductance (G) is the reciprocal of resistance, and it's the ability of a material to conduct electric current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resistance and Conductance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Resistivity and Conductivity
text:
Resistivity and Conductivity

Key terms: resistivity, conductivity, electric current

Resistivity (ρ) is the resistance of a material per unit length and per unit area. Conductivity (σ) is the reciprocal of resistivity, and it's the ability of a material to conduct electric current per unit area and per unit length.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resistivity and Conductivity in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Drift Velocity of Electrons
text:
Drift Velocity of Electrons

Key terms: drift velocity, electric field, electric current

Drift velocity is the average velocity of electrons in a conductor due to an electric field. It's responsible for the net flow of charge, which is the electric current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Drift Velocity of Electrons in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrical Conduction and Ohm's Law
text:
Electrical Conduction and Ohm's Law

Key terms: Ohm's law, resistance, current density

A simple model of electrical conduction explains Ohm's law, where current is directly proportional to voltage and inversely proportional to resistance. This model assumes constant charge and current density.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrical Conduction and Ohm's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electron Drift Speed
text:
Electron Drift Speed

Key terms: drift speed, thermal speed, current density

Electrons in a conductor move with a drift speed, which is much smaller than their thermal speed. This drift speed can be calculated using the formula vd = I / (neA), where I is the current, n is the number density of electrons, e is the elementary charge, and A is the cross-sectional area of the conductor.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electron Drift Speed in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Mobility of Charge Carriers
text:
Mobility of Charge Carriers

Key terms: mobility, drift velocity, electric field

Mobility is the drift velocity of charge carriers per unit electric field. It is defined as μ = vd / E, where vd is the drift velocity, and E is the electric field. Mobility is an important quantity in describing the electrical conductivity of materials.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Mobility of Charge Carriers in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Limitations of Ohm's Law
text:
Limitations of Ohm's Law

Key terms: non-linear, asymmetric, multi-valued

Ohm's law is not valid for all materials and devices. Some materials and devices exhibit non-linear, asymmetric, or multi-valued relationships between voltage and current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Limitations of Ohm's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Resistivity of Materials
text:
Resistivity of Materials

Key terms: conductors, semiconductors, insulators

Materials are classified as conductors, semiconductors, or insulators based on their resistivities. Conductors have low resistivities, insulators have high resistivities, and semiconductors have resistivities that can be decreased by adding impurities or increasing temperature.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resistivity of Materials in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Temperature Dependence of Resistivity
text:
Temperature Dependence of Resistivity

Key terms: temperature coefficient, resistivity, temperature

The resistivity of a material is dependent on temperature. For metals, resistivity increases with temperature, while for semiconductors, resistivity decreases with temperature. The temperature coefficient of resistivity is a measure of this dependence.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Temperature Dependence of Resistivity in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electrical Energy and Power
text:
Electrical Energy and Power

Key terms: electrical energy, power, resistance

Electrical energy is dissipated as heat in a conductor due to collisions of charge carriers with atoms. The power dissipated is given by P = I * V or P = I^2 * R, where I is the current, V is the voltage, and R is the resistance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrical Energy and Power in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Power Dissipation in Resistors
text:
Power Dissipation in Resistors

Key terms: power, voltage, current, resistance

Power (P) dissipated in a resistor is calculated using P = VI, where V is the voltage across the resistor and I is the current through it. The power dissipated in connecting wires (Pc) is given by Pc = I^2 Rc, where Rc is the resistance of the wires.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Power Dissipation in Resistors in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromotive Force (emf) of a Cell
text:
Electromotive Force (emf) of a Cell

Key terms: electromotive force, potential difference, electrode, electrolyte

The electromotive force (emf) of a cell is the potential difference between its positive and negative electrodes in an open circuit. It is given by e = V+ + V-, where V+ and V- are the potential differences between each electrode and the electrolyte.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electromotive Force (emf) of a Cell in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Internal Resistance of a Cell
text:
Internal Resistance of a Cell

Key terms: internal resistance, potential drop, effective emf

The internal resistance (r) of a cell is the resistance of the electrolyte through which the current flows. It causes a potential drop (Ir) across the cell, reducing the effective emf to V = e - Ir.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Internal Resistance of a Cell in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Cells in Series
text:
Cells in Series

Key terms: series, equivalent emf, equivalent internal resistance, current

When cells are connected in series, their equivalent emf (eeq) is the sum of their individual emf's, and their equivalent internal resistance (req) is the sum of their internal resistances. The current through each cell is the same.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Cells in Series in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Cells in Parallel
text:
Cells in Parallel

Key terms: parallel, equivalent emf, equivalent internal resistance, total current

When cells are connected in parallel, their equivalent emf (eeq) is given by 1/eeq = 1/e1 + 1/e2 + ... + 1/en, and their equivalent internal resistance (req) is given by 1/req = 1/r1 + 1/r2 + ... + 1/rn. The total current is the sum of the currents through each cell.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Cells in Parallel in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Kirchhoff's Current Law (Junction Rule)
text:
Kirchhoff's Current Law (Junction Rule)

Key terms: junction, current, conservation of charge

At any junction in an electric circuit, the sum of the currents entering the junction is equal to the sum of the currents leaving the junction. This is a consequence of the conservation of charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Kirchhoff's Current Law (Junction Rule) in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (Loop Rule)
text:
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (Loop Rule)

Key terms: closed loop, potential difference, electric potential

The algebraic sum of the changes in potential around any closed loop involving resistors and cells in the loop is zero. This is a consequence of the fact that electric potential is dependent on the location of the point.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (Loop Rule) in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Kirchhoff's Current Law
text:
Kirchhoff's Current Law

Key terms: junction, current, conservation of charge

At any junction in a circuit, the sum of currents entering the junction equals the sum of currents leaving it. This is based on the conservation of charge.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Kirchhoff's Current Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Kirchhoff's Voltage Law
text:
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law

Key terms: closed loop, potential difference, conservation of energy

The algebraic sum of changes in potential around any closed loop in a circuit must be zero. This is based on the conservation of energy.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Kirchhoff's Voltage Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ohm's Law
text:
Ohm's Law

Key terms: electric current, voltage, resistance

The electric current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage applied across it, provided the temperature and other physical conditions remain constant.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ohm's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Resistivity
text:
Resistivity

Key terms: resistance, resistivity, length, cross-sectional area

The resistance of a material is directly proportional to its length and inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area. This is given by the formula: R = ρl/A, where R is the resistance, ρ is the resistivity, l is the length, and A is the cross-sectional area.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resistivity in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Wheatstone Bridge
text:
Wheatstone Bridge

Key terms: resistor, galvanometer, balance condition, potential difference

A circuit consisting of four resistors and a galvanometer, used to measure an unknown resistance. The bridge is balanced when the galvanometer shows no current, i.e., when the potential difference across the unknown resistor is zero.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Wheatstone Bridge in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Internal Resistance
text:
Internal Resistance

Key terms: source of emf, terminal voltage, current

The resistance of a source of emf (like a battery) to the flow of current within itself. It reduces the terminal voltage of the source when a current is drawn from it.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Internal Resistance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Temperature Coefficient of Resistance
text:
Temperature Coefficient of Resistance

Key terms: resistance, temperature, linear increase

The fractional increase in resistance per unit increase in temperature, in the temperature range where the resistance increases linearly with temperature.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Temperature Coefficient of Resistance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Current Density
text:
Current Density

Key terms: current density, number density, drift velocity, charge, cross-sectional area

The amount of charge flowing per second per unit area normal to the flow. It is given by the formula: j = nevd, where j is the current density, n is the number density of charge carriers, vd is the drift velocity, e is the charge of an electron, and A is the cross-sectional area.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Current Density in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Oersted's Discovery
text:
Oersted's Discovery

Key terms: electric current, magnetic field, Oersted

Hans Christian Oersted discovered that an electric current can deflect a magnetic compass needle, proving the connection between electricity and magnetism.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Oersted's Discovery in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Wire
text:
Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Wire

Key terms: current, magnetic field, wire

A straight, long current-carrying wire produces a circular magnetic field around it, with the wire as the center and the field perpendicular to the wire.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Wire
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Wire in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge
text:
Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge

Key terms: magnetic force, Lorentz force, magnetic field

A moving charge (q) in a magnetic field (B) experiences a force (F) given by F = q(v × B), where v is the velocity of the charge. The force is perpendicular to both v and B.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
text:
Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor

Key terms: magnetic force, current, magnetic field

A current-carrying conductor (I) in a magnetic field (B) experiences a force (F) given by F = Il × B, where l is the length of the conductor. The force is perpendicular to both I and B.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Motion of a Charge in a Magnetic Field
text:
Motion of a Charge in a Magnetic Field

Key terms: magnetic field, charged particle, circular motion

A charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field experiences a force perpendicular to its velocity, causing it to move in a circular or helical path. The radius of the path is given by r = m v / (qB).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Motion of a Charge in a Magnetic Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Motion of a Charge in a Magnetic Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Biot-Savart Law
text:
Biot-Savart Law

Key terms: Biot-Savart law, magnetic field, current element

The magnetic field (dB) at a point due to a current element (Idl) is given by dB = μ₀ (Idl sinθ) / (4πr²), where μ₀ is the permeability of free space, r is the distance from the element, and θ is the angle between r and Idl.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Biot-Savart Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field of a Current Element
text:
Magnetic Field of a Current Element

Key terms: Biot-Savart law, magnetic field, current element

The magnetic field produced by a small current element is given by the Biot-Savart law, which states that the field is proportional to the current, inversely proportional to the square of the distance, and perpendicular to the plane containing the current element and the line connecting it to the field point.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Field of a Current Element
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Field of a Current Element in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field Due to a Current Loop
text:
Magnetic Field Due to a Current Loop

Key terms: current loop, magnetic field, right-hand rule

The magnetic field on the axis of a current loop is given by the Biot-Savart law. The field is zero at the center of the loop and increases linearly with the distance from the center. The direction of the field is given by the right-hand rule: curl your fingers in the direction of the current, and your thumb points in the direction of the field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Field Due to a Current Loop
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Field Due to a Current Loop in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ampere's Circuital Law
text:
Ampere's Circuital Law

Key terms: Ampere's circuital law, magnetic field, current

Ampere's circuital law states that the integral of the magnetic field around a closed loop is equal to the permeability of free space times the total current passing through the surface enclosed by the loop. This law is a useful tool for calculating magnetic fields in situations with symmetry.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Ampere's Circuital Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ampere's Law
text:
Ampere's Law

Key terms: Ampere's Law, magnetic field, enclosed current

Ampere's Law relates the magnetic field to the current enclosed within a loop. It's like Gauss's Law for magnetism.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ampere's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire
text:
Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire

Key terms: magnetic field, long straight wire, current

The magnetic field around a long straight wire carrying a current is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the wire.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid
text:
Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid

Key terms: magnetic field, solenoid, uniform field

The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is uniform and parallel to the axis, given by B = μ₀nI, where n is the number of turns per meter and I is the current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Force Between Two Parallel Currents
text:
Force Between Two Parallel Currents

Key terms: force, parallel currents, attraction

Two parallel currents attract each other. The force per unit length is given by F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/2πd, where d is the distance between the currents.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Force Between Two Parallel Currents in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Torque on a Current Loop
text:
Torque on a Current Loop

Key terms: torque, current loop, magnetic field

A current loop in a magnetic field experiences a torque, given by τ = IABsinθ, where I is the current, A is the area of the loop, and θ is the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the loop.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Torque on a Current Loop in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Moment of a Coil
text:
Magnetic Moment of a Coil

Key terms: magnetic moment, coil, current, area

Magnetic moment (m) of a coil is given by m = NIA, where N is the number of turns, I is the current, and A is the area of the coil. It's a vector quantity that points along the axis of the coil.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Magnetic Moment of a Coil in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Torque on a Current Loop
text:
Torque on a Current Loop

Key terms: torque, current loop, magnetic field, magnetic moment

The torque (τ) on a current loop in a magnetic field (B) is given by τ = m × B, where m is the magnetic moment of the loop. It's a vector quantity that tends to align the loop with the field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Torque on a Current Loop in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Stable and Unstable Equilibrium
text:
Stable and Unstable Equilibrium

Key terms: equilibrium, stable, unstable, magnetic dipole, magnetic field

When a magnetic dipole (m) is in a magnetic field (B), it experiences torque. If m is parallel to B, the equilibrium is stable (any rotation produces a torque that brings it back). If m is antiparallel, the equilibrium is unstable (any rotation increases the torque).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Stable and Unstable Equilibrium in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Cyclotron Frequency
text:
Cyclotron Frequency

Key terms: cyclotron frequency, magnetic field, charged particle, velocity

In a uniform magnetic field (B), a charged particle (q) moving with velocity (v) executes circular motion with a frequency (ν) given by ν = qB/(2πm), where m is the mass of the particle. This is independent of the particle's speed and radius.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Cyclotron Frequency in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Biot-Savart Law
text:
Biot-Savart Law

Key terms: Biot-Savart law, magnetic field, current, distance, angle

The magnetic field (dB) at a point due to an element (dl) of a current-carrying conductor is given by dB = (μ0/4π) * (I dl sinθ/r^2) * hat(r), where I is the current, r is the distance from the element, and θ is the angle between dl and r.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Biot-Savart Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ampere's Circuital Law
text:
Ampere's Circuital Law

Key terms: Ampere's Law, magnetic field, current

States that the integral of the magnetic field over a closed loop is proportional to the current enclosed by the loop. If the magnetic field is tangent and constant along the loop, then the field is directly proportional to the current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ampere's Circuital Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire
text:
Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire

Key terms: magnetic field, current, distance

The magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance R from a long, straight wire carrying a current I is given by B = μ0I/2πR. The field lines are circles concentric with the wire.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Magnetic Field of a Long Straight Wire in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid
text:
Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid

Key terms: magnetic field, solenoid, current, turns per unit length

The magnitude of the magnetic field inside a long solenoid carrying a current I is given by B = μ0nI, where n is the number of turns per unit length.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Force Between Parallel Currents
text:
Magnetic Force Between Parallel Currents

Key terms: magnetic force, parallel currents, anti-parallel currents

Parallel currents attract and anti-parallel currents repel. The force between two parallel currents is proportional to the product of the currents and inversely proportional to the distance between them.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Force Between Parallel Currents in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Moment of a Current Loop
text:
Magnetic Moment of a Current Loop

Key terms: magnetic moment, current loop, turns, area

The magnetic moment m of a planar loop carrying a current I with N turns and area A is given by m = NIA. The direction of m is given by the right-hand thumb rule.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Torque on a Current Loop in a Magnetic Field
text:
Torque on a Current Loop in a Magnetic Field

Key terms: torque, magnetic field, magnetic moment

The torque τ on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field B is given by τ = m × B, where m is the magnetic moment of the loop.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Torque on a Current Loop in a Magnetic Field
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Torque on a Current Loop in a Magnetic Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Moving Coil Galvanometer
text:
Moving Coil Galvanometer

Key terms: moving coil galvanometer, ammeter, voltmeter, shunt resistance, series resistance

A moving coil galvanometer can be converted into an ammeter by introducing a shunt resistance in parallel, or into a voltmeter by introducing a series resistance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Moving Coil Galvanometer in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetism and Lorentz Force
text:
Electromagnetism and Lorentz Force

Key terms: electromagnetism, Lorentz force, electric field, magnetic field

Electrostatic and magnetic fields are linked phenomena (electromagnetism). The Lorentz force F = q(v × B + E) does not imply a universal preferred frame of reference in nature.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electromagnetism and Lorentz Force in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field Lines
text:
Magnetic Field Lines

Key terms: magnetic field lines, closed loops, field strength, intersection

Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops, unlike electric field lines. They represent the direction of the magnetic field and their density indicates the field's strength. Magnetic field lines do not intersect and cannot be created or destroyed.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Field Lines in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Bar Magnet as Equivalent Solenoid
text:
Bar Magnet as Equivalent Solenoid

Key terms: bar magnet, solenoid, circulating currents

A bar magnet can be thought of as a large number of circulating currents, similar to a solenoid. Cutting a bar magnet in half results in two smaller magnets with weaker properties, similar to cutting a solenoid.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Bar Magnet as Equivalent Solenoid in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Dipole in Uniform Field
text:
Magnetic Dipole in Uniform Field

Key terms: magnetic dipole, torque, potential energy, uniform field

A magnetic dipole (like a compass needle) in a uniform magnetic field experiences a torque and potential energy. The torque is maximum when the dipole is perpendicular to the field, and the potential energy is minimum when the dipole is aligned with the field.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Dipole in Uniform Field in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Gauss's Law for Magnetism
text:
Gauss's Law for Magnetism

Key terms: Gauss's law, magnetic flux, closed surface, magnetic monopoles

The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero. This is because isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist, and all magnetic phenomena can be explained in terms of dipoles and current loops.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Gauss's Law for Magnetism in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Gauss's Law for Magnetism
text:
Gauss's Law for Magnetism

Key terms: magnetic flux, closed surface

The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Gauss's Law for Magnetism in Grade 12 Physics.
