text:
Magnetic Field Lines

Key terms: magnetic field lines, direction of magnetic field

Magnetic field lines represent the direction of the magnetic field and cannot emanate from a point or cross each other.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Field Lines in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Dipoles and Current Loops
text:
Magnetic Dipoles and Current Loops

Key terms: magnetic dipoles, current loops

All magnetic phenomena can be explained in terms of an arrangement of dipoles and/or current loops.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Dipoles and Current Loops in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Monopoles
text:
Magnetic Monopoles

Key terms: magnetic monopoles, magnetic charge

If magnetic monopoles existed, Gauss's law of magnetism would be modified to include the magnetic charge enclosed by the surface.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Monopoles in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetisation and Magnetic Intensity
text:
Magnetisation and Magnetic Intensity

Key terms: magnetisation, magnetic intensity

Magnetisation (M) is the net magnetic moment per unit volume, and magnetic intensity (H) is the magnetic field contributed by external factors.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetisation and Magnetic Intensity in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Susceptibility
text:
Magnetic Susceptibility

Key terms: magnetic susceptibility, diamagnetic, paramagnetic

Magnetic susceptibility (χ) is a measure of how a magnetic material responds to an external field, with diamagnetic materials having negative susceptibility and paramagnetic materials having positive susceptibility.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Magnetic Susceptibility in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Diamagnetism
text:
Diamagnetism

Key terms: diamagnetism, magnetic susceptibility

Diamagnetic substances have a tendency to move from stronger to weaker parts of an external magnetic field and have a negative magnetic susceptibility.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Diamagnetism in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Paramagnetism and Ferromagnetism
text:
Paramagnetism and Ferromagnetism

Key terms: paramagnetism, ferromagnetism, domains

Paramagnetic substances have a weak magnetic response to an external field, while ferromagnetic substances have a strong response and form domains of aligned magnetic moments.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Paramagnetism and Ferromagnetism in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ferromagnetic Materials
text:
Ferromagnetic Materials

Key terms: ferromagnetic, domain, hard, soft

Ferromagnetic materials have domains that align in an external magnetic field. They can be hard (retain magnetization) or soft (lose magnetization when field is removed).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ferromagnetic Materials in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Dipole Moment
text:
Magnetic Dipole Moment

Key terms: magnetic moment, current, area, angle

Magnetic moment (m) is a measure of the strength and orientation of a magnet. It's calculated as the product of the current (I), the area (A) of the loop, and the sine of the angle (θ) between the loop's normal and the magnetic field (B).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Dipole Moment in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Field of a Bar Magnet
text:
Magnetic Field of a Bar Magnet

Key terms: magnetic field, bar magnet, distance, formula

The magnetic field (B) of a bar magnet at a distance (r) from its midpoint, where r >> size of the magnet, is given by B = μ₀m / (4πr³) along the axis and B = μ₀m / (2πr³) along the equator.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Magnetic Field of a Bar Magnet
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Magnetic Field of a Bar Magnet in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Gauss's Law for Magnetism
text:
Gauss's Law for Magnetism

Key terms: Gauss's law, magnetic flux, closed loops

Gauss's law for magnetism states that the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero. This means that magnetic field lines form closed loops and never start or end.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Gauss's Law for Magnetism in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Intensity (H) and Magnetization (M)
text:
Magnetic Intensity (H) and Magnetization (M)

Key terms: magnetic intensity, magnetization, magnetic field

Magnetic intensity (H) is the magnetic field (B) divided by the permeability of free space (μ₀). Magnetization (M) is the magnetic moment per unit volume. The magnetic field in a material is given by B = μ₀(H + M).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Intensity (H) and Magnetization (M) in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Materials Classification
text:
Magnetic Materials Classification

Key terms: magnetic materials, magnetic susceptibility, classification

Magnetic materials are classified as diamagnetic, paramagnetic, or ferromagnetic based on their magnetic susceptibility (χ). Diamagnetic materials have χ < 0, paramagnetic have χ > 0, and ferromagnetic have χ >> 0.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Materials Classification in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Permanent Magnets
text:
Permanent Magnets

Key terms: permanent magnets, ferromagnetic, applications

Permanent magnets are substances that retain their ferromagnetic property at room temperature for a long time. They are used in compass needles and other applications.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Permanent Magnets in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Monopoles and Quantization
text:
Magnetic Monopoles and Quantization

Key terms: magnetic monopoles, electric charges, quantization

Magnetic monopoles do not exist, unlike electric charges which are quantized. This leads to continuous magnetic field lines and closed loops.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Magnetic Monopoles and Quantization in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electricity and Magnetism Interrelation
text:
Electricity and Magnetism Interrelation

Key terms: electricity, magnetism, interrelated, electric current, magnetic field

Electricity and magnetism were once thought separate, but experiments showed moving electric charges produce magnetic fields, and moving magnets can induce electric currents.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electricity and Magnetism Interrelation in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Faraday's Discovery
text:
Faraday's Discovery

Key terms: Faraday, discovery, electromagnetic induction, electric current, magnetic field

Michael Faraday discovered that a changing magnetic field can induce an electric current in a wire loop, leading to the development of modern generators and transformers.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Faraday's Discovery in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Flux
text:
Magnetic Flux

Key terms: magnetic flux, magnetic field, area, cosine, angle

Magnetic flux is the product of the magnetic field and the area of a surface, with a cosine term for the angle between them. It's a measure of the magnetic field's effect on a surface.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Flux in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Faraday's Law of Induction
text:
Faraday's Law of Induction

Key terms: Faraday's law, induced emf, magnetic flux, change, oppose

An induced electromotive force (emf) is generated in a closed circuit when there's a change in magnetic flux through the circuit. The induced emf opposes the change that caused it.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Faraday's Law of Induction in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Lenz's Law
text:
Lenz's Law

Key terms: Lenz's law, induced emf, magnetic flux, oppose, energy conservation

Lenz's law states that the polarity of an induced emf is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. This is a principle of conservation of energy.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Lenz's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Lenz's Law
text:
Lenz's Law

Key terms: induced current, magnetic flux, Lenz's law

Lenz's law states that the induced current flows in such a direction that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it. It helps determine the direction of induced current in a conductor.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Lenz's Law in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Motional EMF
text:
Motional EMF

Key terms: motional EMF, magnetic field, velocity

Motional EMF is induced when a conductor moves in a magnetic field. It is given by the formula ε = Blv, where B is the magnetic field strength, l is the length of the conductor, and v is its velocity.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Motional EMF in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Faraday's Law of Induction
text:
Faraday's Law of Induction

Key terms: Faraday's law, induced EMF, magnetic flux

Faraday's law states that the induced EMF (electromotive force) in a closed loop is equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop. It is given by the formula ε = -dΦ/dt.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Faraday's Law of Induction in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Mutual Inductance
text:
Mutual Inductance

Key terms: mutual inductance, inductance, magnetic field

Mutual inductance is a measure of how much a change in current in one conductor induces an EMF in another nearby conductor. It is given by the formula M = µ0n1n2πr2/l, where r is the radius of the coils and l is their length.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Mutual Inductance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Mutual Inductance Formula
text:
Mutual Inductance Formula

Key terms: mutual inductance, permeability, turns, radius, length

Mutual inductance (M) between two coils is given by M = µ0 * µr * n1 * n2 * π * r2 / l, where r is the radius, l is the length, n1 and n2 are the number of turns in each coil, and µ0 and µr are the permeability of free space and the relative permeability of the material between the coils.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Mutual Inductance Formula in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Mutual Inductance Example
text:
Mutual Inductance Example

Key terms: mutual inductance, concentric coils, radius

In two concentric circular coils, the mutual inductance (M) can be calculated using the formula M = π * r1 * r2 / (2 * (r1 + r2)), where r1 and r2 are the radii of the inner and outer coils respectively. This is derived by assuming the magnetic field (B2) to be uniform over the area of the inner coil.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Mutual Inductance Example in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Induced EMF in Coil
text:
Induced EMF in Coil

Key terms: induced emf, mutual inductance, rate of change of current

The induced emf (ε1) in a coil (C1) due to a varying current (I2) in another coil (C2) is given by ε1 = -M * (dI2/dt), where M is the mutual inductance between the two coils. This shows that the induced emf depends on the rate of change of current and the mutual inductance of the two coils.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Induced EMF in Coil in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Self-Inductance Formula
text:
Self-Inductance Formula

Key terms: self-inductance, permeability, cross-sectional area, length, turns per unit length

The self-inductance (L) of a coil is given by L = µ0 * µr * n2 * A / l, where A is the cross-sectional area, l is the length, n is the number of turns per unit length, and µ0 and µr are the permeability of free space and the relative permeability of the material inside the coil.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Self-Inductance Formula in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Self-Induced EMF
text:
Self-Induced EMF

Key terms: self-induced emf, self-inductance, rate of change of current

The self-induced emf (ε) in a coil due to a varying current (I) is given by ε = -L * (dI/dt), where L is the self-inductance of the coil. This shows that the self-induced emf always opposes any change in the current in the coil.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Self-Induced EMF in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Magnetic Energy
text:
Magnetic Energy

Key terms: magnetic energy, self-inductance, current, magnetic field strength

The magnetic energy (U) stored in a solenoid is given by U = (1/2) * L * I2, where L is the self-inductance and I is the current flowing through the solenoid. This energy is proportional to the square of the magnetic field strength (B) and is analogous to the electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Magnetic Energy in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | AC Generator Principle
text:
AC Generator Principle

Key terms: AC generator, induced emf, number of turns, area, magnetic field strength, angular frequency

An AC generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by rotating a coil in a magnetic field. The induced emf (ε) in the coil is given by ε = NBA * ω * sin(ωt), where N is the number of turns, A is the area of the coil, B is the magnetic field strength, and ω is the angular frequency of rotation.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to AC Generator Principle in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Induced EMF in a Loop
text:
Induced EMF in a Loop

Key terms: Faraday's Law, Induced EMF, Solenoid

When the current in a nearby solenoid changes, it induces an EMF in a loop placed inside, according to Faraday's Law of Induction.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Induced EMF in a Loop in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | EMF Induced by Moving Loop
text:
EMF Induced by Moving Loop

Key terms: Induced EMF, Magnetic Field, Velocity, Area

A loop moving out of a uniform magnetic field experiences an induced EMF, which can be calculated using the formula: EMF = B * v * A.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to EMF Induced by Moving Loop in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | EMF Induced by Rotating Rod
text:
EMF Induced by Rotating Rod

Key terms: Induced EMF, Magnetic Field, Length, Angular Frequency

A rotating metallic rod in a uniform magnetic field induces an EMF between its ends, calculated using the formula: EMF = B * l * ω.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to EMF Induced by Rotating Rod in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | EMF Induced in Falling Wire
text:
EMF Induced in Falling Wire

Key terms: Induced EMF, Earth's Magnetic Field, Velocity, Length

A falling wire perpendicular to the Earth's magnetic field induces an EMF, calculated using the formula: EMF = B * v * l.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to EMF Induced in Falling Wire in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Estimating Self-Inductance
text:
Estimating Self-Inductance

Key terms: Self-Inductance, Induced EMF, Time, Current

The self-inductance of a circuit can be estimated using the formula: L = (V * t) / I, where V is the induced EMF, t is the time, and I is the current change.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Estimating Self-Inductance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Mutual Inductance and Flux Linkage
text:
Mutual Inductance and Flux Linkage

Key terms: Mutual Inductance, Flux Linkage, Current

The change in flux linkage (Φ) in a coil due to a changing current in an adjacent coil can be calculated using the formula: Φ = M * I, where M is the mutual inductance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Mutual Inductance and Flux Linkage in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | AC Voltage and Current
text:
AC Voltage and Current

Key terms: AC voltage, amplitude, angular frequency

AC voltage and current vary sinusoidally with time, unlike DC which is constant. AC voltage is represented by v = vm sin(ωt) where vm is amplitude and ω is angular frequency.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to AC Voltage and Current in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Ohm's Law for AC
text:
Ohm's Law for AC

Key terms: Ohm's law, rms value, average power

Ohm's law (i = v/R) applies to AC circuits as well, where v and i are the rms values of voltage and current respectively. The average power in an AC circuit is given by P = I^2R.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ohm's Law for AC in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Inductive Reactance
text:
Inductive Reactance

Key terms: inductive reactance, inductance, phase lag

Inductive reactance (XL = ωL) limits the current in an AC circuit containing an inductor, similar to resistance in a DC circuit. The current lags the voltage by π/2 in a purely inductive circuit.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Inductive Reactance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitive Reactance
text:
Capacitive Reactance

Key terms: capacitive reactance, capacitance, phase lead

Capacitive reactance (XC = 1/(ωC)) limits the current in an AC circuit containing a capacitor. The current leads the voltage by π/2 in a purely capacitive circuit.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Capacitive Reactance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Power in AC Circuits
text:
Power in AC Circuits

Key terms: average power, phase angle, Vm, Im

The average power in an AC circuit containing resistors, inductors, and capacitors can be calculated using the formula P = VmIm cos(θ), where θ is the phase angle between voltage and current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Power in AC Circuits in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitive Reactance
text:
Capacitive Reactance

Key terms: Capacitive Reactance, Frequency, Capacitance, Ohm

The opposition to current flow in a capacitor, inversely proportional to frequency and capacitance, measured in ohms (Ω).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Capacitive Reactance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Current Leading Voltage in Capacitor
text:
Current Leading Voltage in Capacitor

Key terms: Current, Voltage, Capacitor, Phase Difference

In a capacitor circuit, the current leads the voltage by π/2 (90 degrees), meaning the current reaches its peak before the voltage.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Current Leading Voltage in Capacitor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Instantaneous Power in AC Circuit
text:
Instantaneous Power in AC Circuit

Key terms: Instantaneous Power, AC Circuit, Voltage, Current, Phase Angle

The power supplied by an AC source at any instant, calculated as the product of voltage, current, and cosine of the phase angle between them.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Instantaneous Power in AC Circuit in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Average Power in AC Circuit
text:
Average Power in AC Circuit

Key terms: Average Power, AC Circuit, Voltage, Current, Power Factor

The average power dissipated in an AC circuit over a complete cycle, dependent on the voltage, current, and the power factor (cosine of the phase angle).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Average Power in AC Circuit in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Power Factor in AC Circuit
text:
Power Factor in AC Circuit

Key terms: Power Factor, AC Circuit, Average Power, Voltage, Current, Phase Angle

The ratio of the average power dissipated to the product of voltage and current in an AC circuit, equal to the cosine of the phase angle between voltage and current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Power Factor in AC Circuit in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | RMS Voltage and Current
text:
RMS Voltage and Current

Key terms: RMS voltage, RMS current, AC power

RMS (root mean square) voltage and current are special values used to express AC power in the same way as DC power. They are calculated as the square root of the average of the squared instantaneous values over a cycle.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to RMS Voltage and Current in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Inductive Reactance
text:
Inductive Reactance

Key terms: inductive reactance, angular frequency, inductance

Inductive reactance (XL) is the opposition to the flow of AC current caused by an inductor. It is calculated as XL = ωL, where ω is the angular frequency and L is the inductance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Inductive Reactance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Capacitive Reactance
text:
Capacitive Reactance

Key terms: capacitive reactance, angular frequency, capacitance

Capacitive reactance (XC) is the opposition to the flow of AC current caused by a capacitor. It is calculated as XC = 1/(ωC), where ω is the angular frequency and C is the capacitance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Capacitive Reactance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Impedance
text:
Impedance

Key terms: impedance, resistance, inductive reactance, capacitive reactance

Impedance (Z) is the total opposition to the flow of AC current in a circuit, taking into account resistance (R), inductive reactance (XL), and capacitive reactance (XC). It is calculated as Z = √(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2).

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Impedance in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Power Factor
text:
Power Factor

Key terms: power factor, real power, apparent power, phase difference

Power factor is the ratio of the real power (P) to the apparent power (S) in an AC circuit. It is a measure of how effectively the circuit uses the power supplied to it. It is calculated as power factor = P/S or cosφ, where φ is the phase difference between voltage and current.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Power Factor in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Wattless Current
text:
Wattless Current

Key terms: wattless current, power factor

Wattless current is the current in a purely inductive or capacitive circuit that does not dissipate any power. It is the current that flows when the power factor is zero, i.e., cosφ = 0.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Wattless Current in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Transformer Voltage Ratio
text:
Transformer Voltage Ratio

Key terms: transformer voltage ratio, secondary voltage, primary voltage, number of turns

The voltage ratio of a transformer is the ratio of the secondary voltage (Vs) to the primary voltage (Vp). It is calculated as Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, where Ns is the number of turns in the secondary coil and Np is the number of turns in the primary coil.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transformer Voltage Ratio in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Transformer Current Ratio
text:
Transformer Current Ratio

Key terms: transformer current ratio, secondary current, primary current, number of turns

The current ratio of a transformer is the ratio of the secondary current (Is) to the primary current (Ip). It is calculated as Is/Ip = Np/Ns, where Ns is the number of turns in the secondary coil and Np is the number of turns in the primary coil.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transformer Current Ratio in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | AC Ampere Definition
text:
AC Ampere Definition

Key terms: alternating current, Joule heating, ampere

The ampere for alternating current (AC) is defined based on Joule heating, as the force between wires carrying AC currents averages to zero.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to AC Ampere Definition in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Adding AC Voltages
text:
Adding AC Voltages

Key terms: AC voltage, phase, RC circuit

In an AC circuit, when adding voltages across different elements, consider their phases. For example, in an RC circuit, VR + VC should be calculated as VR * cos(θ) + VC * cos(θ + π/2).

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Phasors in AC Circuits
text:
Phasors in AC Circuits

Key terms: phasor, harmonically varying scalar, vector addition

Phasors represent the amplitude and phase of harmonically varying scalars (like voltage and current) using rotating vectors for easy addition.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Phasors in AC Circuits in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Power Losses in AC Circuits
text:
Power Losses in AC Circuits

Key terms: power loss, resistive element, AC circuit

Only the resistive element in an AC circuit dissipates energy and causes power losses. Pure capacitances and pure inductances do not.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Power Losses in AC Circuits in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Resonance in RLC Circuits
text:
Resonance in RLC Circuits

Key terms: resonance, RLC circuit, XL, XC

Resonance in an RLC circuit occurs when XL = XC, i.e., ωL = 1/(ωC). Both L and C elements are necessary for resonance.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Resonance in RLC Circuits in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Power Factor in RLC Circuits
text:
Power Factor in RLC Circuits

Key terms: power factor, RLC circuit, maximum power

Power factor in an RLC circuit indicates how close the circuit is to expending maximum power, i.e., how efficiently it's working.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Power Factor in RLC Circuits in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Energy Transformation in Generators/Motors
text:
Energy Transformation in Generators/Motors

Key terms: generator, motor, energy transformation

Generators and motors transform energy from one form to another. In a motor, electric energy is input, and mechanical energy is output. In a generator, it's the opposite.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Energy Transformation in Generators/Motors in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Transformer Operation
text:
Transformer Operation

Key terms: transformer, voltage change, conservation of energy

A transformer changes the voltage level (step-up or step-down) without violating the law of conservation of energy. The current changes inversely with the voltage change.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transformer Operation in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Displacement Current
text:
Displacement Current

Key terms: displacement current, Maxwell, Ampere's law

A current caused by a changing electric field, proposed by Maxwell to resolve inconsistencies in Ampere's law. It's the reason for electromagnetic waves.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Displacement Current in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Maxwell's Equations
text:
Maxwell's Equations

Key terms: Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, electric field, magnetic field

A set of equations that describe the fundamental properties of electric and magnetic fields and their interactions. They predict the existence of electromagnetic waves.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Maxwell's Equations in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetic Waves
text:
Electromagnetic Waves

Key terms: electromagnetic waves, accelerated charges, electric field, magnetic field

Waves that consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation. They are produced by accelerated charges.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electromagnetic Waves in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Sources of Electromagnetic Waves
text:
Sources of Electromagnetic Waves

Key terms: sources of electromagnetic waves, accelerated charges, oscillating electric circuit

Accelerated charges, like those in an oscillating electric circuit, can produce electromagnetic waves. Stationary or uniformly moving charges cannot.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Sources of Electromagnetic Waves in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Nature of Electromagnetic Waves
text:
Nature of Electromagnetic Waves

Key terms: nature of electromagnetic waves, Maxwell's equations, electric field, magnetic field

Electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation. They can be shown using Maxwell's equations.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Nature of Electromagnetic Waves in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Hertz's Experiment
text:
Hertz's Experiment

Key terms: Hertz's experiment, Maxwell's theory, electromagnetic waves

Hertz's successful experimental test of Maxwell's theory, demonstrating the existence of electromagnetic waves in the radio wave region.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Hertz's Experiment in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Bose's Experiment
text:
Bose's Experiment

Key terms: Bose's experiment, electromagnetic waves, short wavelengths

Bose's experiment, following Hertz's work, produced and observed electromagnetic waves of much shorter wavelengths in the laboratory.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Bose's Experiment in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Marconi's Experiment
text:
Marconi's Experiment

Key terms: Marconi's experiment, communication, electromagnetic waves

Marconi's experiment marked the beginning of communication using electromagnetic waves, transmitting them over long distances.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Marconi's Experiment in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetic Wave Propagation
text:
Electromagnetic Wave Propagation

Key terms: electric field, magnetic field, propagation, speed of light

Electromagnetic waves consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and the direction of propagation. They travel at a speed of c (3x10^8 m/s) in vacuum.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Displacement Current
text:
Displacement Current

Key terms: displacement current, electric field, Maxwell's equations

Displacement current is a term used in Maxwell's equations to account for the time-varying electric field. It's given by the formula ∇⋅E = ρ/ε₀.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Displacement Current in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetic Spectrum
text:
Electromagnetic Spectrum

Key terms: electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength, frequency

The electromagnetic spectrum includes various types of waves like radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays, each with different wavelengths and frequencies.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electromagnetic Spectrum in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Hertz's Contribution
text:
Hertz's Contribution

Key terms: Hertz, electromagnetic waves, Maxwell's theory

Hertz was the first to produce and detect electromagnetic waves in the laboratory, verifying Maxwell's theory and paving the way for modern communication technologies.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Hertz's Contribution in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetic Wave Equations
text:
Electromagnetic Wave Equations

Key terms: electromagnetic wave equations, wave number, angular frequency, speed of light

The equations for electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave are E = E₀ sin(kz - ωt) and B = B₀ sin(kz - ωt), where k is the wave number, ω is the angular frequency, and c is the speed of light.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electromagnetic Wave Equations in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetic Wave Speed in Vacuum
text:
Electromagnetic Wave Speed in Vacuum

Key terms: speed of light, permeability, permittivity

The speed of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by the formula 1/√(μ₀ε₀), which equals the speed of light (c = 3x10^8 m/s).

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electromagnetic Wave Speed in Vacuum in Grade 12 Physics.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Physics | Electromagnetic Wave Energy Transfer
text:
Electromagnetic Wave Energy Transfer

Key terms: energy transfer, radio waves, light

Electromagnetic waves can carry energy from one place to another, as seen in radio and TV signals, light from the sun, and other applications.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electromagnetic Wave Energy Transfer in Grade 12 Physics.

text:
Electromagnetic Wave Equation

An electromagnetic wave's electric and magnetic fields vary sinusoidally, with the same frequency and wavelength, and are perpendicular to each other and the direction of wave propagation.

metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electromagnetic Wave Equation in Grade 12 Physics.

text:
Speed of Electromagnetic Waves

The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum (c) is a constant, equal to the speed of light, and is related to the free space permeability and permittivity constants.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Speed of Electromagnetic Waves in Grade 12 Physics.

Electromagnetic Wave Spectrum

Electromagnetic waves have a wide range of wavelengths and frequencies, with different regions having specific names and interactions with matter.

text:
Electromagnetic Wave Interaction with Matter

Electromagnetic waves interact with matter via their electric and magnetic fields, causing charges to oscillate. The interaction depends on the wave's wavelength and the nature of the matter.

Infrared Waves and Heat

Infrared waves, with lower frequencies than visible light, can vibrate entire atoms or molecules, increasing the internal energy and temperature of a substance.
